About ACCTA

A professional body established to promote excellence, integrity and professionalism in the practice of tax advisory services.

WHO WE ARE

Developing, regulating and recognising competent tax professionals.

ACCTA sets high professional and ethical standards, develops globally aligned qualifications, and fosters continuous professional development among its members. Through education, research and advocacy, it seeks to enhance the quality and credibility of tax advisory services delivered to individuals, businesses and public institutions. The Association awards the Certified Chartered Tax Advisor (CCTA) qualification. Members adhere to a strict Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct and engage in ongoing learning to maintain their professional competence.

VISION

To be a globally respected institute advancing excellence and integrity in tax advisory.

MISSION

To develop competent, ethical, and globally recognised tax advisors while safeguarding the public interest.

IntegrityExcellenceIndependenceAccountabilityTransparencyPublic InterestInnovationCollaboration

OBJECTIVES

What the Association exists to do

01

Promote professional excellence

The highest standards of competence, integrity and ethical conduct among Certified Chartered Tax Advisors.

02

Advance the tax advisory profession

Develop, regulate and strengthen the profession in line with national and international best practice.

03

Safeguard the public interest

Tax advice delivered in a way that protects the public and supports sound tax governance.

04

Education and qualification

Design, award and regulate the CCTA qualification and other approved programmes.

05

Continuing professional development

Lifelong learning through mandatory CPD, training, seminars and workshops.

06

Ethics and professional conduct

Establish, monitor and enforce a code of ethics for all members.

07

Research and knowledge

Research, publications and thought leadership in taxation and public finance.

08

Representation and advocacy

Represent members in consultations with government and regulators.

09

International collaboration

Relationships with local, regional and international professional bodies.

10

Capacity building

Build tax advisory capacity among practitioners, institutions and the community.

FUNCTIONS

How we deliver those objectives

Membership regulation

Admit, classify and register members; keep the register of members in good standing.

Examinations

Conduct examinations and set standards for entry, progression and certification.

Disciplinary oversight

Investigate complaints and impose disciplinary measures.

CPD administration

Prescribe CPD requirements and monitor compliance.

Guidance and standards

Issue technical guidance, practice notes and standards.

Education and training

Courses, conferences, workshops and webinars.

Publications

Journals, newsletters, research papers and professional materials.

Stakeholder engagement

Work with tax authorities, policymakers, academia and industry.

Accreditation

Recognise educational programmes and training partners.

OUR EMBLEM

Protection, strength and balance

The shield stands for trust and institutional authority. The central pillar stands for strength, stability and enduring principles. The scales stand for fairness, equity and impartial judgment between taxpayer and state.

Navy — trust, credibility
Maroon — integrity, leadership
White — clarity, transparency

COMMITTEES

Standing committees of the Council

MPC

Membership and Professional Conduct

Members Development (CPD, seminars, recruitment) and Ethics & Professional Conduct (disciplinary matters, professional practice) sub-committees.

LTE

Learning, Testing and Evaluation

Curriculum, programme delivery and examinations.

BPR

Business Promotion and International Relations

MOUs, collaboration with schools, universities and professional bodies, international promotion.

RTC

Research and Technical

International Tax Conclave, Journal of Compliance Management, technical papers, Tax Case Law book and Tax Manual.

FOC

Finance and Operations

Finance and day-to-day operation of the Secretariat. Chaired by the President.

PATRON

A distinguished individual who lends moral authority and high-level guidance, supports advocacy, and attends convocations and milestone events. Not involved in day-to-day management.

ADVISORY BOARD

Appointed by the Council for up to two years to advise on strategy. The Council seeks its views but is not bound by them.
